def:boltzmann-constant: Definition Boltzmann constant in QOU natural units. In QOU natural units the Boltzmann constant is k_B := 1.
rem:boltzmann-constant-motivation:
Remark Why the Boltzmann constant is set to unity. The convention of def:boltzmann-constant is chosen as follows. The quantum ideal gas law (see quantum ideal gas law) gives P_q V_q = N T_q = N \hbar_q at leading order. The classical form is PV = N k_B T.

In this framework, the temperature T_q = \hbar_q (quantum temperature) naturally carries units of energy. It is the Reeb tick rate, not a statistical parameter. Comparing the two forms, the choice consistent with T_q = \hbar_q is:

  N \, k_B \, T_q \;=\; N \, \hbar_q
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  k_B \;=\; 1.

The constant can be set to unity because the temperature is defined in energy units. One requires no separate conversion factor for a "degrees of freedom" temperature scale.

In SI units, physical temperature T_{\mathrm{phys}} is measured in kelvin, and k_B = 1.381 \times 10^{-23} J/K provides the energy conversion. At the comparison with measurement, the reading is k_B T_{\mathrm{phys}} = \hbar_q. The thermal energy per degree of freedom precisely equals the quantum Planck constant.

With the quantum temperature T_q = \hbar_q, the thermal energy is

  k_B \, T_q = T_q = \hbar_q = \frac{q-1}{q}.
rem:gas-constant-derivation:

  \mathfrak{m}_{C\text{-}12}(q) = \frac{12\,\mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) + 6\,\delta_{\mathfrak{n}} - B_{12}(q)}{\hbar_q^2}.

Here \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 7.32772\ldots represents the Borromean volume, \delta_{\mathfrak{n}} is the neutron--proton Skein mass difference, and B_{12}(q) is the nuclear binding energy evaluated from the 66-crossing transfer matrix.

The gas constant strictly evaluates to:

  R_q = \frac{12\,\hbar_q^3}{12\,\mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) + 6\,\delta_{\mathfrak{n}} - B_{12}(q)}.

At leading order, neglecting binding energy and neutron mass corrections, this simplifies to:

  R_q \approx \frac{(q-1)^3}{q^3 \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)}.

The gas constant R requires precisely two inputs: the algebraic parameter q and the topological invariant \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3). Because the mass predictions match CODATA to sub-keV precision, R is structurally guaranteed to be correct. It sits strictly downstream of the mass spectrum.

ex:hydrogen-partition-function:
Example Partition function for monatomic hydrogen. Setup. Consider a monatomic hydrogen gas comprising N atoms of \mathcal{A}(1,0) at quantum temperature T_q = \hbar_q in a region U with quantum volume V_q. Each hydrogen atom combines a proton (Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 with Hopf binding \mathcal{L}_H) and an electron (trefoil T_{2,3}). One treats the atom as a single composite knot K_H = \mathcal{A}(1,0). This supplies the simplest non-trivial gas. Hydrogen possesses the lightest knot structure and fewest internal degrees of freedom.

Single-atom partition function. The atom K_H resides in an S^3 fibre. Its internal degrees of freedom dictate the partition function:

  1. Translational: the brane point p \in U where the atom sits, yielding a factor of |U|.
  2. Rotational: the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) orientation of the Borromean link within the fibre. The q-angular momentum eigenvalues are J_q^2 = [j]_q [j+1]_q. The rotational partition function is
  z_q^{(\mathrm{rot})} = \sum_{j=0}^{j_{\max}} [2j+1]_q e^{-\beta_q \, [j]_q [j+1]_q \, \hbar_q}.
  1. Vibrational: the writhe of the braid closure governing q-momentum p_q(\beta). The amphichiral Borromean link exhibits writhe w(\mathcal{B}_3) = 0. The translational kinetic contribution vanishes identically at lowest order.
  2. Internal (action): the categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q(K_H) = \mathrm{tr}_\tau(\rho(\beta_H)). This supplies the rest-mass contribution.

The single-atom partition function evaluates to:

  z_q = e^{-\beta_q \, \mathfrak{S}_q(K_H)} \cdot z_q^{(\mathrm{rot})} \cdot z_q^{(\mathrm{vib})},

where z_q^{(\mathrm{vib})} = 1 + O(\hbar_q^2). The vanishing writhe suppresses the leading vibrational mode.

N-atom gas. The quantum ideal gas law governs the macro-state:

  P_q \, V_q = N \, \hbar_q \left( 1 + \frac{\hbar_q^2}{[2]_q} \,\mathfrak{S}_q(K_H) \right).

The correction term \hbar_q^2 \, \mathfrak{S}_q(K_H) / [2]_q measures the ratio of the q-anomaly energy to the fibre volume. For a hypothetical unknot gas, this correction vanishes, reproducing the exact leading-order law P_q V_q = N \hbar_q.

Simplicity of hydrogen. Among all atoms \mathcal{A}(Z, N):

  • Hydrogen possesses the simplest knot: one Borromean link paired with one trefoil, yielding composite crossing number n_K = 13.
  • The amphichiral Borromean link (w = 0) zeroes the leading-order momentum contribution.
  • The proton mass dominates. The term \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) / \hbar_q^2 accounts for \sim 99.95\% of the atomic mass. The electron trefoil T_{2,3} acts as a torus knot with \mathrm{Vol}(T_{2,3}) = 0, contributing zero hyperbolic volume. Its mass arises entirely from vacuum drag.

Heat capacity. The constant-volume heat capacity emerges from C_V = -\beta_q^2 (\partial^2 \ln Z_q / \partial \beta_q^2). At low temperature, only the j = 0 rotational mode populates, sending C_V \to 0. At high temperature, all rotational modes contribute, driving C_V \to \frac{3}{2} N \hbar_q. This recovers the classical equipartition result C_V = \frac{3}{2} N k_B for three rotational degrees of freedom. The crossover occurs at the rotational temperature T_q^{(\mathrm{rot})} = [1]_q [2]_q \, \hbar_q^2.
sec:phase-transitions-intro:
The quantum ideal gas law yields a partition function whose dominant saddle point sits inside one Hecke channel of H_n(q). Phase transitions represent the loci where this dominance shifts. One derives critical temperatures using the S^3 boundary action. This restricts the categorical action to the Hopf base S^2 of the fibration S^1 \hookrightarrow S^3_q \to S^2. The quantities [2]_q and [n_K]_q control the transition boundaries T_q^{(g \to l)} and T_q^{(l \to s)}.

One maps gas, liquid, and solid states onto the symmetric, mixed, and antisymmetric Hecke channels, locating the triple point. Sublimation (the direct solid--gas transition) is recorded without a derivation: the Hecke channels are complementary summands rather than an extension of one by another, so \mathrm{Ext}^1_{H_n(q)} supplies no obstruction to the liquid phase. One presents an observational test of the Z-parity sublimation rule, establishing a metallic-bonding test that separates sublimation from continuous condensation. Finally, one establishes the boundary action as a canonical example of degree-0 opacity.
prop:phase-transition-boundary:
Proposition Phase transitions as S^3 boundary actions. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with N particle knots in a region U. A phase transition occurs at a critical temperature T_q^{(c)}. At this temperature, the dominant saddle point of the partition function Z_q jumps discontinuously between topologically distinct sectors of \mathrm{Conf}(U).

The S^3 boundary action dictates the critical temperatures. It restricts the categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q to the Hopf base S^2 of the fibration S^1 \hookrightarrow S^3_q \to S^2:

  \mathfrak{S}_q^{(\partial)} = \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Ad}} \!\oint_{S^2} \omega_{\mathcal{F}} \,\wedge\, *\eta_q,

This is the non-abelian Stokes surface integral of the adjoint connection.

The gas--liquid critical temperature is

  T_q^{(g \to l)} = \frac{\mathfrak{S}_q^{(\partial)}}{[2]_q}.

The liquid--solid critical temperature is

  T_q^{(l \to s)} = \frac{\mathfrak{S}_q^{(\partial)}}{[2]_q \cdot [n_K]_q},

where n_K denotes the crossing number of the particle knot.

Sublimation represents a direct solid--gas transition. It occurs when the intermediate liquid phase is not populated at any temperature between the two critical values.

No Hecke extension class obstructs that phase, because there are no non-split extensions here to carry one. The symmetric and antisymmetric channels are the q- and -q^{-1}-eigenspaces of the braiding \sigma (The Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q) as a categorical quotient), and the eigenprojections

  e_{+} = \frac{\sigma + q^{-1}}{[2]_q},
  \qquad
  e_{-} = \frac{q - \sigma}{[2]_q}

are orthogonal idempotents summing to 1 whenever [2]_q is invertible — the same condition the two critical temperatures above already require, since they divide by it. So V^{\otimes 2} = S^2 V \oplus \Lambda^2 V is a direct sum, not an extension. For general n the conclusion follows instead from semisimplicity: at a substrate parameter that is not a root of unity, H_n(q) is semisimple (Complete decomposition of the tensor tower(1)), so every short exact sequence of H_n(q)-modules splits and \mathrm{Ext}^1_{H_n(q)} vanishes on every pair of modules.

Over the Laurent ring \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], where [2]_q is not invertible, extensions of the antisymmetric channel by the symmetric one are classified by \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] / ([2]_q) \cong \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] / (q^2 + 1) \cong \mathbb{Z}[i]. That group is supported on q^2 = -1, which no real q meets, so the archimedean realisation never leaves the split case. What selects sublimation over a stable liquid phase is left open.
conj:composite-crossing-parity:
Conjecture Sublimation from shell-filling representation theory. Conditional on the Borromean-quark conjecture. Let \mathcal{A}(Z, N) be a stable atom with electron configuration occupying shells S_1, \ldots, S_k. The complete decomposition

  V^{\otimes n} \cong \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n,\, \ell(\lambda) \leq 2} V_\lambda \otimes S_\lambda

rem:composite-crossing-sublimation-crite:
Remark Sublimation, crossing parity, and the full phase criterion. The single Hecke algebra H_n(q) of Sublimation from shell-filling representation theory governs the phase behaviour through the following criteria.

Sublimation criterion. There is no split/non-split dichotomy to state this criterion in. At a substrate parameter that is not a root of unity H_n(q) is semisimple, so every short exact sequence of H_n(q)-modules splits and \mathrm{Ext}^1_{H_n(q)} vanishes on every pair of modules (Phase transitions as S^3 boundary actions); the S_\lambda are irreducible summands of V^{\otimes n} (Complete decomposition of the tensor tower(1)), and an irreducible module is not an extension of anything by anything.

What is left is a correlation with the Young diagram of the valence shell, stated without a mechanism. The liquid phase is stable when the outermost electron shell is closed or nearly closed — in terms of partitions, when the diagram \lambda_{\mathrm{outer}} labelling the valence electrons satisfies \lambda_1 - \lambda_2 \leq 1, so that the valence shell inhabits the symmetric or near-symmetric sector of the Schur--Weyl decomposition. Sublimation is instead associated with a half-filled valence shell (\lambda_1 \approx \lambda_2 + n/2), where the mixed Hecke channel achieves maximal dimension. That dimension statement is a fact about S_\lambda; the step from it to a thermodynamic instability is not supplied here.

Crossing parity. To estimate sublimation behavior, one examines the composite crossing parity. The composite crossing number identically satisfies n_K(\mathcal{A}) \equiv Z \pmod{2}, stemming from the crossing budget A^2 + 7A + 5Z and the invariant parity A(A+1) \equiv 0 \pmod{2}. This parity detects the mod-2 shadow of the Young diagram structure. It acts as a necessary but not sufficient condition for sublimation, as it fails to distinguish closed shells from half-filled ones.

Full criterion. Let \ell_v denote the number of valence electrons beyond the last closed shell. Let \ell_{\max} dictate the capacity of the valence shell (\ell_{\max} = 2n^2 for principal quantum number n). One systematically classifies the macroscopic phase:

  1. Closed shell (\ell_v = 0 or \ell_v = \ell_{\max}): The liquid phase is stable.
  2. Near-closed shell (\ell_v = 1 or \ell_v = \ell_{\max} - 1): The liquid phase is stable.
  3. Half-filled shell (\ell_v \approx \ell_{\max}/2) with odd Z: The atom is structurally prone to sublimation.
  4. Metallic band (delocalized electrons): The single-atom Hecke module S_\lambda expands to the band-structure module \bigoplus_k S_{\lambda(k)} over crystal momenta k, and the liquid phase is stable.

The classification is empirical: nothing above derives it from the Hecke representation theory.
rem:phase-transition-interpretation:
Remark Three phases from Hecke channels and the triple point. The Hecke algebra H_n(q) carries irreducible representations corresponding to Young diagrams. At a generic temperature T_q, a single representation dominates the partition function. At a critical temperature T_q^{(c)}, two representations contribute equally, introducing a non-analyticity into the partition function.

The three phases.

  1. Gas (symmetric channel, eigenvalue q). At high T_q, each knot confines to a single S^3 fibre. The equation of state mirrors the quantum ideal gas law.
  2. Liquid (mixed channel). At intermediate T_q, knots initiate Hopf-linking across fibres through the Hopf base S^2. This inter-fibre linking establishes structural correlations.
  3. Solid (antisymmetric channel, eigenvalue -q^{-1}). At low T_q, inter-fibre links dominate. Knots form a rigid braid lattice, occupying the strict sign representation.

Sublimation mechanism. The Hecke algebra supplies no mechanism. The three channels are complementary summands, not an extension of one by another: at a substrate parameter that is not a root of unity H_n(q) is semisimple, so every short exact sequence of H_n(q)-modules splits and no extension class distinguishes an unstable liquid phase from a stable one (Phase transitions as S^3 boundary actions). The correlation with odd crossing number recorded in Sublimation, crossing parity, and the full phase criterion stands on its own arithmetic and carries no derivation from here.

Triple point. All three phases coexist only when three Hecke representations contribute identically. This defines a rigid codimension-2 condition in the (T_q, P_q) plane. It obeys the Gibbs phase rule.

Classical theory comparison. Classical theory generates phase transitions artificially by appending ad hoc inter-particle potentials (van der Waals or Lennard-Jones) to the ideal gas. The QOU generates physical interactions through inter-fibre braid linking across the Hopf base of S^3_q. The S^3 topology supplies the binding potential via its boundary action. The Hecke representation theory dictates the exact discrete phase structure.
rem:crossing-parity-test:
Remark Observational test of the Z-parity sublimation rule. The full sublimation criterion structurally relies on the Hecke representation structure, avoiding mere crossing parity. The determining variable strictly equals the valence electron count \ell_v relative to the shell capacity \ell_{\max}.

Test against observed sublimation at 1 atm. See Table.

Score: 11/12 (92%). The representation-theoretic criterion cleanly resolves all three counterexamples where the crude parity rule fails:

  • H (\ell_v = 1 of \ell_{\max} = 2): The shell rests near-closed. The extension splits via the trivializing section. Liquid H exists at 20 K. \checkmark
  • Na (\ell_v = 1 of \ell_{\max} = 2): The shell rests near-closed and explicitly exhibits metallic band delocalization. It melts normally. \checkmark
  • Cu (3d^{10}4s^1): The 3d subshell closes perfectly. The single 4s valence electron rests near-closed and acts metallic. It melts normally. \checkmark

The molecular exception: iodine. Iodine (\ell_v = 5 of \ell_{\max} = 6) holds a near-closed shell. The atomic criterion structurally predicts a stable liquid, yet iodine sublimes at 1 atm. This exception manifests strictly because iodine forms a molecular I_2 van der Waals solid. The weak intermolecular binding artificially renders sublimation favorable. The single-atom Hecke module represents the wrong fundamental unit. The I_2 dimer holds crossing number n_K(I_2) \equiv 0 \pmod{2}, but the inter-dimer linking remains too weak to stabilize a liquid phase. The sublimation behaves molecularly, not atomically.

Connection to magic numbers. The decomposition V^{\otimes n} \cong \bigoplus_\lambda V_\lambda \otimes S_\lambda generates the nuclear magic numbers (2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126) exactly via palindromic Poincaré polynomials in the Bruhat lattice. The identical decomposition identically derives the sublimation criterion via Ext groups between the irreducible summands S_\lambda. Magic shell closures smoothly trivialize the extension; half-filled shells ruthlessly maximize it.

def:van-der-waals-hopf-channel:
Definition The Hopf symmetric block e_+ — retained cosh carrier (not van der Waals). In the 2-strand inter-molecular Hecke algebra H_2(q), the symmetric (Hopf) block is the idempotent

  e_+ = \frac{\sigma + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}, \qquad \sigma \mapsto q \ \ (\text{trivial rep}),

the Hopf /[2]_q block. Its complement is the directional (hydrogen-bond) block e_- = (q-\sigma)/(q+q^{-1}) (sign rep, \sigma\mapsto -q^{-1}).
rem:van-der-waals-hopf-channel-remark:
Remark The Hopf channel and the van der Waals force. The Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H = T_{2,2} = \widehat{\sigma_1^2} possesses vanishing hyperbolic volume, \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{L}_H)=0. This dictates a volume-less correlation. Two molecules link without bonding; they share no bonded volume. This establishes the topological mechanism of dispersion (the van der Waals force): attraction without a chemical bond. Within this Hopf channel, the symmetric e_+ block constitutes the retained [2]_q / diquark carrier. The van der Waals force itself is not e_+. It acts strictly as the bar-odd residual \sinh(2\lambda)(e_+-e_-) that the canonical P_{\mathrm{avg}} projection structurally discards. The dispersion force represents an explicit small object, not an unmodelled residual.

The block represents a genuine Wedderburn projector: e_+ + e_- = 1 and e_+^2 = e_+. The Hopf link is not a separate operator from e_\pm. In H_2(q), \sigma_1^2 = (q-q^{-1})\sigma_1 + 1 sits algebraically dependent on \{1,\sigma_1\}. The operator-selection SDP over \{1,\sigma_1,\sigma_1^2\} acts rank-deficient. The fundamentally independent blocks remain exactly e_+ (the symmetric Hopf-diquark carrier) and e_- (the antisymmetric directional block). Van der Waals is strictly the bar-odd combination \sinh(2\lambda)(e_+-e_-) of these two blocks, never either block alone.
prop:hopf-link-symmetric-decomposition:
Proposition Hopf-link symmetric decomposition: \sigma_1^2 = q^2 e_+ + q^{-2} e_-. The Hopf element \sigma_1^2 of H_2(q) formally weights the two blocks by their squared eigenvalues:

  \sigma_1^2 = q^2 e_+ + q^{-2} e_-.

Equivalently, cleared of the [2]_q = q+q^{-1} denominator:

  [2]_q \sigma_1^2 = q^2 (\sigma_1+q^{-1}) + q^{-2} (q-\sigma_1).

This formally derives from the Hecke relation \sigma_1^2 = (q-q^{-1})\sigma_1 + 1.

Its value at q_0 and the van der Waals reading are recorded in this remark.

prop:vdw-pskew-isolation:
Proposition Van der Waals as the bar-odd (P_{\mathrm{skew}}, sinh) channel. Under the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1}, the Hopf weighting identically splits into a bar-even and a bar-odd part. With rapidity \lambda = \ln q:

rem:vdw-pskew-isolation-interpretation:

The van der Waals residual operates as a real observable residing strictly in the discarded sector. A non-zero \mathrm{Im}(q) initiates a distinct, later refinement, safely separate from this channel.

This witnesses a section of A_0 outside the reach of any finite braid. Remark: Incompleteness as degree-0 opacity: the Turing--Goedel--horizon triangle interprets the diagonal as a degree-0 vanishing locus. Remark: Statistical mechanics as the polynomial observable subcategory confines the framework to the polynomial-bandwidth observables of \S 1. Remark: The information paradox as a theorem of arithmetic concludes by equating the black-hole information paradox with Goedel incompleteness operating on Hawking quanta. The next section, Horizons and Aeons, adopts the computational horizon as the prototype for every jet horizon in the descended universe.
prop:incompleteness-implies-horizon:
Proposition Turing completeness with \mathbb{N}-embedding implies non-empty computational horizon. Let (P, e, \mathrm{eval}) denote a Turing-complete resolution system:

  • P forms a set of programs (finite braids).
  • e \colon \mathbb{N} \twoheadrightarrow P provides a surjective enumeration (the braid group on finitely many strands is countable).
  • \mathrm{eval} \colon P \to (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}) maps each program to its computed total function.

There exists a function f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} outside the image of \mathrm{eval}:

  \exists\, f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N},\;
  \forall\, p \in P,\;
  \mathrm{eval}(p) \neq f.

The computable fragment is strictly smaller than the full function space.
prf:incompleteness-implies-horizon:
Proof Proof of incompleteness implies horizon. Define the diagonal function:

  d(n) = \mathrm{eval}(e(n))(n) + 1.

For any program p \in P, surjectivity provides an index n such that e(n) = p. Then:

  d(n) = \mathrm{eval}(p)(n) + 1 \neq \mathrm{eval}(p)(n).

Consequently, d \neq \mathrm{eval}(p). Because p was arbitrary, d \notin \mathrm{im}(\mathrm{eval}). \square

Necessity of \mathbb{N}-embedding.

The diagonal argument builds d by evaluating program e(n) on input n. This self-application imposes two requirements:

  1. Countability of programs: The map e must surject from \mathbb{N} onto P, indexing programs by natural numbers. In the QOU, the braid group B_n on n strands is finitely generated and thus countable. The set of all finite braids \bigsqcup_n B_n forms a countable union of countable sets, satisfying the requirement.

  2. \mathbb{N} as input domain: Programs must compute functions \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}, requiring the system to represent and manipulate natural numbers. The QOU satisfies this via Turing completeness (Skein Turing machine). Each Toffoli gate acts on bit strings (\{0,1\}^n \hookrightarrow \mathbb{N}), and the Skein polynomial evaluates to values that distinguish inputs.

If programs are uncountable, or if the system cannot represent \mathbb{N}, the diagonal construction fails. The computable fragment might then span the entire function space. A trivial category (one object, one morphism) remains vacuously "Turing-complete," but it hosts no non-computable sections because it lacks arithmetic encoding.

Connection to the computational horizon.

Each non-computable function d corresponds to a section E_d \in \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) that evades factorization through any finite braid (non-computable bundles). These sections populate the computational horizon \mathcal{H}_c = V(\mathfrak{h}_c) (computational horizon):

  E_d \in \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) \setminus \Gamma_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{S}, A_0)
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathcal{H}_c \neq \varnothing.

The proposition ensures that such E_d exist whenever the system meets arithmetic non-triviality. The computational horizon is therefore a necessary feature of any Turing-complete resolution system equipped with \mathbb{N}-embedding: it follows from the system's expressive power alone, independent of any specific NP-complete link.
rem:incompleteness-horizon-nontriviality: Remark Arithmetic non-triviality condition on the resolution system. The hypothesis of Turing completeness with \mathbb{N}-embedding implies non-empty computational horizon carries an implicit arithmetic non-triviality condition: the surjectivity of e and the domain \mathbb{N} of \mathrm{eval} require \mathbb{N} to embed into the system. Without this condition the diagonal argument is vacuous — a trivial category lacks self-referential capacity, rendering incompleteness inapplicable.
rem:stat-mech-computational-horizon:
Remark Statistical mechanics as the polynomial observable subcategory. The quantum ideal gas law,

  P_q \, V_q
  \;=\; N \, T_q
  \left(
    1 + \frac{\hbar_q^2}{[2]_q}\,\langle \mathfrak{S}_q \rangle
  \right),

is a degree-0 section of an exponentially complex partition function. The partition function Z_q = (|U| \cdot z_q)^N / N! sums over all N! braid permutations of N knot configurations across |U| fibres. Through F_q = -T_q \ln Z_q and Stirling's approximation, the equation of state collapses this exponential sum into a single polynomial relation among three observables: (P_q, V_q, T_q).

This constitutes the Markov trace of statistical mechanics. Just as the Markov trace collapses 3^c resolution paths to a Skein polynomial, the free energy collapses N! microstate configurations to an equation of state.

PV = NkT is in the polynomial horizon. The full dictionary:

See Table.

The equation of state is computationally extractable in polynomial time. The \ln Z_q calculation factors through Stirling's approximation, reducing the N!-fold sum to O(N \log N) operations. This reduction precisely matches the condition for membership in \mathcal{R}^{\circ}, the polynomial observable subcategory.

The q-correction is degree-1 leakage. The correction term \hbar_q^2 \langle \mathfrak{S}_q \rangle / [2]_q represents the first piece of boundary information crossing from the microstate into the macroscopic equation. It originates from the S^3 boundary action. The Frobenius pairing at \partial U generates a non-trivial d_q^2 correction entirely missed by a purely degree-0 classical computation.

In jet-tower language, the classical limit PV = NkT is strictly degree-0. The quantum correction forms the degree-1 term. It is structurally analogous to Hawking radiation leaking through the jet horizon.

Phase transitions are horizon crossings. At the critical temperature T_q^{(c)}, the dominant Hecke representation abruptly jumps, and the free energy develops a sharp non-analyticity. This constitutes a computational horizon in the (T_q, P_q) plane. The degree-0 section (the bulk phase of the system) becomes discontinuous. Simultaneously, degree \geq 1 data—such as correlations and critical exponents—varies continuously across the boundary.

The three macroscopic phases (gas, liquid, solid) correspond to three connected components of the polynomial observable subcategory in configuration space. These are distinct aeons of the partition function, separated by rigid phase boundaries where the dominant degree-0 algebra predictability vanishes and replaces itself.

Statistical mechanics evaluates the polynomial observable subcategory. The apparatus of statistical mechanics functions purely as technology for extracting degree-0 and low-degree sections from exponentially large configuration spaces. It exists strictly because observers are polynomial-time, probing an exponentially complex microstate.

Any Turing-complete system with an \mathbb{N}-embedding inevitably generates non-computable sections. Statistical mechanics describes computation from the polynomial side of that boundary. It is an unavoidable approximation, enforced by the computational horizon, designed to extract the accessible degree-0 truth while discarding the uncomputable exponential remainder.

rem:information-paradox-incompleteness:
Remark The information paradox as a theorem of arithmetic. One reframes the black hole information paradox as a question of arithmetic rather than gravity. The incompleteness--horizon identification provides the bridge.

The horizon as syntax boundary. One treats the horizon as a syntax boundary. Behind it lie sections that exist as well-defined semantic elements of the full algebra \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0). However, no finite braid computation from outside can derive them. They are syntactically unprovable. This instantiates the categorical reading of Gödel: existence without provability characterises the boundary. The Bekenstein–Hawking entropy counts only the degree-1 witnesses that leak across, not the hidden degree-0 truth.

The paradox. A black hole interior is a region where A_0 = 0. The degree-0 sections describing particle identities, crossing structures, and fibre values inside the horizon exist in \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0). But they do not belong to \Gamma_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{S}, A_0): no finite braid computation from outside the horizon produces them.

This mirrors a Gödel sentence, which is true in the model but unprovable from the accessible axioms.

One maps the three standard positions on the information paradox to positions on incompleteness:

Position Information paradox Incompleteness analog
Information is destroyed Sections in the interior have no algebraic meaning Gödel sentences are neither true nor false (rejected by standard model theory)
Information is preserved but inaccessible Sections exist but cannot be computed from outside Gödel sentences are true but unprovable (the standard reading)
Information escapes via Hawking radiation Degree \geq 1 data gradually reconstructs degree-0 truth Partial witnesses accumulate toward a proof that never terminates

One adopts the second position. Three physics references bear on this choice. Harlow and Hayden argue that extracting the relevant information from the radiation takes time exponential in the entropy of the black hole [arxiv-1301.4504v4, §3.4], a computational form of "preserved but inaccessible". Susskind and Thorlacius show by a gedanken experiment that an observer who samples the Hawking radiation and then crosses the horizon cannot discover the duplicated information inside the black hole before reaching the singularity [susskind-thorlacius1993], so no single observer sees the information both preserved and accessible. Lowe, Polchinski and Susskind argue that the standard argument for information loss assumes the effective theory outside the horizon is a local quantum field theory, and give evidence from string theory that this locality fails across the horizon [arxiv-hep-th-9506138v1]; the second position therefore carries a cost in locality. The algebra A is well-defined everywhere, including behind the horizon, but no finite sequence of Planck steps from the outside can reach it.

The Bekenstein--Hawking entropy as a Gödel count. The Bekenstein--Hawking entropy S = A / (4\ell_P^2) counts the dimension of \Gamma(\mathcal{H}, A_1/A_0), the independent degree-1 sections on the horizon surface. These are the verifiable partial evidence, thermal leakage, and NP witnesses accessible from the outside.

The degree-0 sections behind the horizon remain uncounted by the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy. The entropy counts proof fragments, not theorems.

  S_{\mathrm{BH}}
  \;=\;
  \dim \Gamma(\mathcal{H},\, A_1/A_0)
  \;=\;
  \text{number of witnessable facts}
  \;\neq\;
  \dim \Gamma(\mathcal{H},\, A_0)
  \;=\; 0.

The entropy scales with area because the degree-1 space is rich. The degree-0 space is empty because no complete truths cross the boundary. This asymmetry characterises any formal system powerful enough to encode self-referential computation.

Aeon boundaries as Gödel boundaries. This identification extends to cosmological horizons. An aeon boundary is a locus where A_0 = 0. Degree-0 sections vanish, and the observable subcategory \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} terminates. The Big Bang state is one such boundary: the universe begins with no degree-0 data and accumulates it through Planck-step computation.

Each aeon acts as a consistent theory: a connected component of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} where degree-0 sections are non-trivial and the Frobenius pairing is non-degenerate. The aeon boundary is the expressive limit where Gödelian sentences reside. Crossing an aeon boundary transitions to a stronger theory. The degree \geq 1 data from the dying aeon seeds the axioms of the next.

The universe iterates past its own incompleteness rather than resolving it. Each aeon is a consistent fragment bounded by the limit of finite derivation.
sec:horizons-aeons-intro:
The incompleteness horizon of the previous section remains local to a single resolution tree. One now globalises it. The brane tower A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots stratifies every affine chart by jet order. A horizon forms as a codimension-1 locus where the lowest floor A_0 vanishes, allowing higher floors to leak through. This section defines these horizons, organises their connected components into aeons, and links the resulting cyclic structure to Penrose's Conformal Cyclic Cosmology.

Definition: Jet horizon (degree-0 vanishing locus) establishes the horizon ideal \mathfrak{h} \subset \Gamma(U, A_0). It dictates that photons remain blocked at the horizon, while degree \geq 1 Taylor coefficients escape. Definition: Big bang state (degree-0 trivial configuration) reframes this condition as an initial datum. Definition: CMB as boundary datum of a big bang state isolates the surviving degree-1 and degree-2 jet data. Remark: The CMB as photon color content surviving the horizon interprets this data as photon polarization and color content. Remark: Hawking radiation as degree \geq 1 leakage recovers the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy as the rank of \Gamma(\mathcal{H}, A_1/A_0).

Categorical packaging follows. Definition: Observable subcategory \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)) isolates the locus where A_0 does not vanish. Definition: Aeon identifies a connected component of that subcategory. Definition: Horizon functor and Definition: CMB functor map each aeon to its boundary and its surviving jet data. The Conjecture: Aeon recycling: \Phi_1^q \circ \mathrm{CMB} lands in \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} posits that the boundary datum regenerates a chart under one Planck step of the torsion flow. Proposition: Conformal invariance at the jet horizon and Proposition: A QOU with aeons is a conformal cyclic cosmology align this structure with Penrose's framework. Remark: Relation to Penrose's Conformal Cyclic Cosmology supplies the required translation dictionary. The next section, Quantum Geometry Variants, applies the aeon boundary and degree-0 vanishing to model alternative Euler-characteristic scenarios for the descended universe.
def:jet-horizon:
Definition Jet horizon (degree-0 vanishing locus). Let U \subset M_0 be an open subset of the descended universe carrying an affine chart, and let A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots be the brane tower.

A jet horizon in U is a closed codimension-1 subset \mathcal{H} \subset U such that every section of A_0 extending continuously across \mathcal{H} vanishes on \mathcal{H}:

  \mathcal{H}
  = 
  V\!\bigl(\mathfrak{h}\bigr),
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{h}
  = 
  \bigl\{
    s \in \Gamma(U, A_0)
     : 
    s|_{\mathcal{H}} = 0
  \bigr\}.

The ideal \mathfrak{h} \subset \Gamma(U, A_0) is the horizon ideal.
rem:jet-horizon-remark:
Remark What crosses a jet horizon. At degree 0, no fibre data crosses \mathcal{H}: photons (K = \mathbf{1}_{B_4} 4-strand id, step 0) cannot propagate across the horizon, and no zeroth-order observable distinguishes one side from the other.

Higher-degree leakage. The horizon ideal lives strictly in A_0. The quotient algebras A_k / A_0 for k \geq 1 are not constrained by \mathfrak{h}. First-order (linear) and second-order (curvature) jet data can carry non-trivial sections across \mathcal{H}.

Jet degree Data type Crosses \mathcal{H}?
0 Fibre value (photon identity) No
1 Linear transport (winding number) Yes
2 Curvature (linking number) Yes
\geq 3 Higher-order topology Yes

The information that leaks through a jet horizon is exactly the degree \geq 1 jet data: the Taylor coefficients of the energy function beyond the constant term. This leakage is thermal in character. It carries no particle identity (degree 0), only statistical correlations (degrees 1 and 2).
def:big-bang-state:
Definition Big bang state (degree-0 trivial configuration). Let U \subset M_0 be an affine chart carrying a bundle initial condition \mathcal{S}_0 = \sum_i (p_i, H_i). Then \mathcal{S}_0 is a big bang state if its degree-0 algebra is trivial:

  \Gamma\!\bigl(U, A_0|_{\mathcal{S}_0}\bigr) = 0.
rem:big-bang-state-remark: Remark Constituents and jet data of a big bang state. Equivalently, every constituent of a big bang state \mathcal{S}_0 satisfies H_i = \varnothing (a photon with zero fibre data), and the section s_0 \in \Gamma(U, A_0) encoding their identity vanishes. There are no degree-0 observables at \mathcal{S}_0. The remaining higher-jet data—sections of A_1/A_0 (linear transport) and A_2/A_0 (curvature)—provides the seed for the forward light cone \mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2, \ldots
rem:big-bang-state-jet-horizon:
Remark Big bang state versus jet horizon: same vanishing A_0, different role; existence is dynamical. Relation to the jet horizon. A big bang state is algebraically identical to the data on one side of a jet horizon . Both are characterised by the vanishing of A_0. The difference is purely contextual:

Concept Algebraic condition Role
Jet horizon A_0\vert_{\mathcal{H}} = 0 Boundary within an affine chart
Big bang state A_0\vert_{\mathcal{S}_0} = 0 Reference configuration of an affine chart

A jet horizon is a boundary. A big bang state is an initial condition. The same vanishing ideal \mathfrak{h} describes both.

Existence is not assumed. Whether any affine chart in the descended universe admits a big bang state is a dynamical question, not an axiom. The framework accommodates three consistent scenarios:

  • Every affine chart has a big bang state (global initial singularity).
  • Only some charts have a big bang state.
  • No chart has a big bang state (the backward light cone extends indefinitely).
def:cmb-boundary-datum:
Definition CMB as boundary datum of a big bang state. The cosmic microwave background records the initial state of an aeon. One models this as the boundary jet data surviving at a big bang state.

Let \mathcal{S}_0 be a big bang state in an affine chart U. Let A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots be the associated brane tower . The cosmic microwave background (CMB) of \mathcal{S}_0 is the boundary datum

  \mathrm{CMB}(\mathcal{S}_0)
  = 
  \bigl(
    \Gamma(U, A_1/A_0)|_{\mathcal{S}_0}, 
    \Gamma(U, A_2/A_0)|_{\mathcal{S}_0}
  \bigr).

This pair isolates the degree-1 (linear transport) and degree-2 (curvature) jet data at \mathcal{S}_0. Because A_0|_{\mathcal{S}_0} = 0, one can equivalently restrict A_1 \oplus A_2:

  \mathrm{CMB}(\mathcal{S}_0)
   \cong 
  \bigl(A_1 \oplus A_2\bigr)\big|_{\mathcal{S}_0}.

The jet degrees dictate the physical content.

Degree Jet data Physical content
1 A_1/A_0: linear transport Photon polarization modes (\sigma_0, \sigma_1), winding numbers, first-order correlations
2 A_2/A_0: curvature Hopf-link cross-terms (L_{\pm}), linking numbers, power spectrum

Because degree-0 data (A_0) vanishes at the boundary, the CMB lacks photon identity \mathbf{1}, particle labels, and knot types. It is strictly thermal. It carries only the color content (\varphi_0, \varphi_1) of the boundary photons .

When \mathcal{S}_0 bounds the past of an aeon \mathcal{A} , the CMB seeds the forward light cone. The initial Planck step \mathcal{S}_0 \to \mathcal{S}_1 generates particles. It applies the Reeb flow f_q to the degree-1 transport data, regenerating non-trivial degree-0 data.

When \mathcal{S}_0 also bounds the future of a preceding aeon \mathcal{A}', the datum inherits from the terminal horizon of \mathcal{A}' . The thermal remnant of one aeon becomes the initial condition of the next.
rem:cmb-photon-color-content:
Remark The CMB as photon color content surviving the horizon. One decomposes a photon into identity and color components. The photon color content model writes a photon as:

  \gamma
  = 
  \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1
  + \varphi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1},
  \qquad \varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_{01} \in R.

Here \mathbf{1} is the degree-0 photon identity, \sigma_0, \sigma_1 are the Hecke generators, and \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_0\sigma_1 - h\sigma_0 is the chiral pair-production vertex (photon). Each generator maps to a polarization mode on the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). The generator \sigma_0 provides horizontal polarization; \sigma_1 provides vertical.
rem:hawking-radiation:
Remark Hawking radiation as degree \geq 1 leakage. The jet horizon provides an algebraic model of a black hole event horizon.

Hawking radiation [hawking1975] predicts that black holes emit thermal radiation at temperature T_H = \hbar c^3 / (8\pi G M k_B). This radiation carries no internal information. It exhibits a Planck spectrum determined entirely by the mass M.

The jet-horizon framework translates this into a direct algebraic interpretation:

  1. Degree-0 data is trapped. The horizon ideal \mathfrak{h} \subset A_0 blocks all zeroth-order sections. No particle identity (knot type or crossing structure) crosses the horizon. This states the information paradox algebraically: the full fibre data of A_0 remains inaccessible from the outside.

  2. Degree \geq 1 data leaks. The quotients A_1/A_0 and A_2/A_0 carry non-trivial sections across \mathcal{H}. These constitute the first and second Taylor coefficients of the energy function (linear transport as winding number, curvature as linking number). This data is thermal. It depends on statistical properties (temperature \sim \eta_q, operational entropy ) rather than individual particle states.

  3. The Bekenstein--Hawking entropy [bekenstein1973] S = A / (4\ell_P^2) counts the independent degree \geq 1 sections on the horizon surface \mathcal{H}. In the QOU framework, the area A is the rank of \Gamma(\mathcal{H}, A_1/A_0). This rank measures the dimension of the first-order jet data that the horizon can support.

  4. No photons escape. Photons are degree-0 objects (K = \varnothing, step 0 in the jet-Planck correspondence ). The horizon ideal blocks them alongside all other degree-0 data. What an external observer detects as "thermal photons" are actually degree-1 winding modes lacking knot identity. These are the Hawking quanta.
rem:incompleteness-horizon:
Remark Incompleteness as degree-0 opacity: the Turing--Gödel--horizon triangle. The QOU is Turing-complete: every finite computation encodes as a braid, every braid closes to a link, and the Skein polynomial acts as the output (Skein Turing machine). By Gödel's first incompleteness theorem [goedel1931], any consistent formal system expressive enough to encode its own arithmetic contains true statements that evade finite derivation. Turing's reformulation [turing1936] sharpens this: decision problems exist whose halting behaviour no finite algorithm can determine.

In the QOU, Turing completeness, Gödel incompleteness, and black hole information loss are not independent. They arise as three projections of a single algebraic phenomenon: the vanishing of degree-0 sections.

The triangle.

Vertex Statement Algebraic form
Turing completeness Every computable function is a finite braid Sections factoring through finite \beta \in B_n span \Gamma_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{S}, A_0)
Gödel incompleteness There exist true statements unprovable by finite derivation \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) \supsetneq \Gamma_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{S}, A_0): the full section space strictly contains the computable fragment
Black hole information loss Degree-0 data cannot cross the horizon \Gamma(\mathcal{H}, A_0) = 0: degree-0 sections vanish on \mathcal{H}

These three vertices share a common mechanism: the categorical distinction between degree-0 data (the answer, truth value, or particle identity) and degree \geq 1 data (the witness, proof sketch, or thermal radiation).

Incompleteness is horizon non-emptiness.

A section E \in \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) that does not factor through any finite braid (non-computable bundles) constitutes a degree-0 truth that no finite computation can yield. It acts as a Gödelian sentence. The locus of all such sections is precisely the computational horizon \mathcal{H}_c = V(\mathfrak{h}_c) (computational horizon). This horizon defines the frontier of the polynomial observable subcategory \mathcal{R}^{\circ}:

  \text{G\"{o}del sentence}
  \;\;\longleftrightarrow\;\;
  E \in \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) \setminus
    \Gamma_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{S}, A_0)
  \;\;\longleftrightarrow\;\;
  E\big|_{\mathcal{H}_c} = 0.

A true-but-unprovable statement thus functions as a degree-0 section that vanishes on the computational boundary. It persists in the full algebra but remains invisible to any polynomial-time observer.

The physical horizon as incompleteness.

The jet horizon \mathcal{H} = V(\mathfrak{h}) (jet horizon) enforces identical opacity for physical observers. The Bekenstein--Hawking entropy counts independent degree \geq 1 sections on \mathcal{H} (Hawking radiation). It counts no degree-0 data, because none survives. An observer outside a black hole occupies the exact position of a Turing machine confronting a Gödelian sentence: degree \geq 1 evidence (witnesses, thermal radiation) leaks across the boundary, but the degree-0 truth (the answer, the particle identity) remains formally inaccessible.

The information paradox [hawking1975] asks whether information is lost or merely hidden. In the incompleteness framing, the answer is structural:

  • The information exists (the section resides in \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0)).
  • It cannot be extracted by any finite computation from outside the horizon (it vanishes on \mathcal{H} or \mathcal{H}_c).
  • It can be partially witnessed via degree \geq 1 leakage (Hawking quanta, NP witnesses).

The information is neither "lost" nor "preserved" operationally. It is incomplete. The system is expressive enough to state the truth, but lacks the strength to derive it from the accessible side of the boundary.

Self-reference and the necessity of horizons.

Gödel's theorem requires self-reference: the system must encode statements about itself. The QOU meets this requirement via Turing completeness; the Skein-braid encoding empowers the universe to simulate its own dynamics. Self-reference exacts a cost: any system modeling itself must contain true-but-inaccessible states. These states form the horizon.

The argument is linear:

  1. The QOU is Turing-complete (q \neq 1 suffices: substrate computation).
  2. It can therefore encode self-referential statements (programs analysing their own Skein polynomials).
  3. By Gödel--Turing, degree-0 sections exist that no finite braid produces.
  4. These sections populate the computational horizon \mathcal{H}_c.
  5. The computational horizon is structurally identical to the jet horizon \mathcal{H} (dictionary).
  6. Therefore, a Turing-complete universe necessarily manifests horizons.

The black hole is not an accident of general relativity: it follows from any universe expressive enough to encode arithmetic. Any universe with q \neq 1 — where Toffoli gates carry non-zero amplitude — must host regions where degree-0 truth remains inaccessible.
def:observable-subcategory:
Definition Observable subcategory \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)). Let \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)) be the category of finite bundles over the projective line, whose morphisms are permutation-isotopy pairs. The observable subcategory \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)) is the full subcategory on the objects whose degree-0 algebra is non-trivial:

  \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)) = \bigl\{ \mathcal{S} \in \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)) : \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) \neq 0 \bigr\}.
rem:observable-subcategory-remark:
Remark Observability, complement and components of the observable subcategory. Observability. One requires a non-degenerate Frobenius pairing to define degree-0 measurements. When A_0|_{\mathcal{S}} = 0, the pairing degenerates on the lowest floor of the brane tower and no degree-0 observable is well-defined. The subcategory \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} defines the regime where the full observational apparatus functions.

Complement. The complement \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)) \setminus \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)) consists of configurations with A_0 = 0. These are the jet horizons and big bang states.

Connected components. The connected components \pi_0(\mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}) are the aeons. Each aeon is a maximal connected full subcategory of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}. It encompasses all light cones accessible without crossing a jet horizon.
def:aeon: Definition Aeon. Let \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)) be the observable subcategory of the category of finite bundles over the projective line. An aeon is a connected component of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)).
rem:aeon-remark:
Remark Aeons as unions of light cones. An aeon \mathcal{A} is a maximal full subcategory of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} such that a zigzag of morphisms (flow maps, inclusions, or their inverses) connects any two objects \mathcal{S} and \mathcal{S}' without leaving \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}. Every light cone forms a directed diagram within the aeon. The aeon unions all light cones that connect without crossing a jet horizon.

Maximality. The connected-component definition guarantees maximality automatically. No larger subcategory of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} containing \mathcal{A} is connected. One avoids defining an explicit interval (a, b) \subset \mathbb{Z}. Instead, one defines the aeon over the full categorical structure, naturally encompassing all intersecting light cones.
def:aeon-boundary:
Definition Boundary of an aeon. Let \mathcal{A} be an aeon —a connected component of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)).

The boundary \partial\mathcal{A} of an aeon is the set of objects \mathcal{S} \in \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)) that are limits of diagrams in \mathcal{A} but do not themselves lie in \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}:

  \partial\mathcal{A}
  = 
  \overline{\mathcal{A}} \setminus \mathcal{A}^{\circ}
  \subset
  \bigl\{
    \mathcal{S} : \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) = 0
  \bigr\}.

Each boundary object represents a jet horizon or a big bang state . One defines the boundary datum at \mathcal{S} \in \partial\mathcal{A} as the colimit of the degree \geq 1 data over all diagrams in \mathcal{A} approaching \mathcal{S}. This is the CMB boundary datum \mathrm{CMB}(\partial\mathcal{A}) .
